protocolFindings.finding: A historical transcript alone is insufficient for full v1 conformance. Capture-time producers must seal the base repository tree, Task bytes, Executor Agent identity, Runtime Specification, result manifest, and native trace.

Hosted model services cannot normally be content-addressed by the producer. The protocol therefore requires precise provider and deployment identification plus any available attestation, while reserving independently reproducible status for executions whose dependencies are recoverable or faithfully substitutable.
A review of an earlier patch must not be treated as an evaluation of later result bytes. Result subjects make this distinction enforceable.
A safe task-relevant projection can be much smaller than a field-for-field scrub, but it must be labeled as a lossy derived trace and cannot replace the private native trace commitment.

The current entropy detector rejects public technical identifiers in this fixture, including an exact pinned version inside the Result patch. A publish path must distinguish content identifiers and structured technical names from credentials without rewriting Result bytes.
